pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_billiards.en: Pool
Controls (1)
Pool is a game in which players use the white (cue) ball to knock balls 1 through 15 into the pockets of the table. There are three rule sets: "Nine-ball," "Rotation," and "Eight-ball."
To shoot the cue ball use
To adjust your position and change the point where the cue ball is struck use
Pool
Controls(2)
If you pocket a ball (or balls) you can take another shot.
It is considered a foul if you pocket the cue ball or if the cue ball fails to hit any balls.
When there is a foul, the opposing player is free to take a shot after placing the cue ball anywhere on the table.
Pool
Rules forNine-ball
Nine-ball uses balls 1 through 9.
Players must pocket the balls on the table in order, starting with the lowest-numbered ball. The player who pockets the 9 ball first is the winner.
All balls pocketed on a foul (except for the 9 ball) remain pocketed, and the game continues.
Pool
RulesforRotation
Rotation uses balls 1 through 15. Players must pocket the balls on the table in order, starting with the lowest-numbered ball.
Pocketing a ball awards the player with the same number of points as the ball's number.
pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_billiards.juego: Pocketing a ball awards the player with the same number of points as the ball's number.

pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_billiards.en: The first player to exceed 61 points is the winner.
If all balls are expended without any player exceeding 61,
the balls are racked again and play continues from a break shot.
Pool
Rules of Eight-ball (1)
Eight-ball uses balls 1 through 15.
Balls are divided into two groups: balls 1 through 7 are "Low Balls" and balls 8 through 15 are "High Balls."
The first ball that is pocketed after the break shot determines the group you will be targeting.
pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_billiards.juego: The first ball that is pocketed after the break shot determines the group you will be targeting.

pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_billiards.en: Pool
Rules of Eight-ball (2)
To win, you must pocket the 8 ball after pocketing all of the balls in your group. You can pocket the balls in your group in any order.

the pocket that you will be aiming for. If the 8 ball falls into a different pocket, you immediately lose. Pocketing the 8 ball before all of the balls in your group have been sunk also counts as a loss.
Pool
Trick Shots
Occasionally, there are circumstances where a ball can not be sunk conventionally. In such cases, the following trick shots are possible:
Combination Shot · Carom Shot · Kiss Shot
Pool
Combination Shot:

Say you would like to pocket ball A. Instead of striking ball A directly with the cue ball, you hit ball B, which in turn hits ball A. Pocketing a ball in this manner is referred to as a Combination Shot.
Pool
Carom Shot:

Say you would like to pocket ball A. Instead of striking ball A directly with the cue ball, you hit ball B first, after which the cue ball rebounds and strikes ball A. Pocketing a ball in this manner is referred to as a Carom Shot.
Pool
Kiss Shot:

Say you would like to pocket ball A. You strike ball A directly with the cue ball, after which it changes its path by ricocheting off ball B. Pocketing a ball in this manner is referred to as a Kiss Shot.
Pool
Rules of Four-ball (1)
Four-ball is played on a table without pockets, known as a carom billiards table.
Four balls (two cue balls and two red balls) are used. The player who goes first uses a white cue ball, and the other player uses a yellow cue ball.
A point is scored by caroming on two or more object balls. The opponent's cue ball is also considered an object ball. No point is scored when object balls collide.
Pool
Rules of Four-ball (2)
A player who scores gets to shoot again. When no point is scored, it becomes the other player's turn to shoot. The first player to reach the designated score wins.
Anchor Spaces

The four corners of a carom billiards table have an area known as an anchor space, outlined in red. If there are two or more object balls in a single anchor space, a foul results if more than one remains after two shots.

pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_blackjack.en: Blackjack
BasicRules
The object of the game is to obtain a hand total that is closest to 21.
If your hand is closer to 21 than the dealer's, you win. If your hand
exceeds 21, you bust and automatically lose.
Card Values
The player can choose whether to count an ace as 1 or 11. The 10, J, Q, and K cards all have a value of 10.
or11
Blackjack
Blackjack
A combinationof an ace and a card with thevalueof 10 iscalled
Blackjack,and hasthehighesthandvalue.Aslongasthedealer doesn't have Blackjack as well, you are paid 2.5 times your stake.
Terminology (1)
·Hit: ·Stand: .Split:
Add an additional card to your hand. Remain with the current hand.
If the first two cards you receive are of the same value,
you may split the cards to create two hands.
· Double Down:After seeing the first two cards, you may double
your bet (double down). You must then draw a third card.
Blackjack
Terminology (2)
·Surrender: A declaration of surrender. Since half of your stake is
returned to you, this option is useful when there appears to be no chance of victory.
· Insurance: Available when the dealer's revealed card is an ace.
You can purchase insurance for the price of half your stake. In the event that the dealer holds a Blackjack, you lose your stake but receive twice what you paid as insurance.
Blackjack

·Six Under: This is achieved if you choose to be hit four times and
receive a total of six cardswithoutbusting.Six Under counts asanautomaticvictory.
Green Card
A green card is contained within the deck. When this card appears, the deck is shuffled together with the cards that have alreadybeen used.

pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_chinchiro.en: Cee-lo
How to Play:Getting Started
Cee-lo is a four-player game played with three dice.
Three dice are rolled. In the event that two numbers match, the third, non-matching number becomes the "point." Players compete for the highest point.
Cee-lo
How toPlay:Points
A point's numerical value determines its strength. 6 is the strongest and 1 is the weakest. If you win with points 1 through 6, the return is the same as your stake.
If you do not establish a point after three rolls, it is
counted as an automatic loss. If any of the dice fly out of the bowl, it is counted as "missing the pot," whichisalsoanautomaticloss.
There are a number of additional combinations that hold special values.
Cee-lo
How to Play: Special Combinations
Trips Achieved by rolling three dice of the same number. Trips consisting of numbers 2 through 6 triple your stake. Trips of all 1's is called an "ace out" and quintuples your stake.
Achieved with a combination of 4, 5, and 6. Doubles your stake.
Achieved with a combination of 1, 2, and 3. However, the combination results in a loss of double your stake.
Cee-lo
How to Play: Special Combinations
Musashi :
Rolling 6, 3, and 4 has the same value as getting a 6, but doubles the amounts won or lost.
All-odds Rolling 1, 3, and 5 counts the same as the previous player's roll. Counts as a 3 when rolled by the first player or banker.
All-evens: Rolling 2, 4, and 6 will count the same as the next player's roll. Counts as a 4 when rolled by the first player or banker.
Cee-lo
HowtoPlay:Steps
1. First, a banker is selected. The remaining players place their bets, which the banker meets.
2. The banker throws the dice first, followed by each
player. Bets are settled after all throws have been completed.
However, the outcome of the game is decided on the spot if the banker rolls one of the combinations on the next page.

becomes the new banker. Like before, the banker rolls first, followed by the players, until the game is set.
The game ends when all players have been banker or if a player runs out of chips.
Cee-lo

pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_mjrule0.d.en: Four players compete to be the first to complete a 14-tile hand. This hand is typically composed of 4 groups of 3-tile combinations and 1 pair.
The pointvalue of a player'shand is determined by the tiles they have collected.For a list of mahjong hands,please refer to Hands.
Each player takes turns drawing and discarding tiles to construct their hand to reach the win condition. In addition to drawing them, players can stealcertaintiles thattheir opponents discard.

pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_mjrule1.d.en: A game of mahjong consists of 136 tiles. There are exactly 4 copies of each tile, resulting in 34 unique tiles.
Tiles: Numbers 1-9 of 3 different suits: Circles, Bamboo,& Characters 4 Wind tiles (East, South,West,North)
The Wind and Dragon tiles are collectively referred to as honor tiles. Tiles 1 and 9 of each suit are referred to as terminal tiles.

pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_mjrule10..en: As you play through a game, you will draw and discard tiles while trying toformsetsofstraightsand three-of-a-kindstomeetthewincondition. Sometimes you can steal from others players to reach that goal quicker.

Aim to form 4 sets of three (straights or triplets) and 1 pair, but do note thattherearealternatewinconditions,suchasSevenPairs,ormore advanced hands such as Thirteen Orphans,which have higher point values.

pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_mjrule11..en: Immediately after an opponent discards a tile, you can claim and add it to your hand, creating a "meld." Melds are divided into pon, chi, and kan, explained on the next page.
Several scoring elements are only valid in concealed hands and others are reduced in value when a player has one or more exposed melds, so remember, steal wisely.

pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_mjrule12..en: that tile can be claimed and melded to form a set by selecting "Chi." You canonlysteala tilefromtheopponentsittingtoyourleftforthismeld.

pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_mjrule13..en: If you manage to draw all 4 of the same tile, you can declare a concealed kan. This differs from the normal one in that your hand is still technically concealed, and you reap the benefits of making a kan.
If you have a concealed hand that needs only one more tile to win, you

can declare "Riichi" by paying 1,oo0 points. However, you will not be able to change the tiles in your hand and are forced to discard any draws that are not your winning tile. The advantage of declaring Riichi is the potential to increase thevalue of yourhand.

pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_mjrule14..en: Each round of mahjong has a tile representing the dora. By having your hand consistoftilesthatcorrespond to thedorasrevealed,youcan increase the valueofyourhand;it canpotentially turn a mediocre hand intoa high-value hand!
The dora is the indicator's succeeding tile.

pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_mjrule15..en: In this example, the dora is 2 bamboo since the tile revealed is the 1 bamboo.

pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_mjrule16..en: There are two ways to complete a hand: ron and tsumo.
* Ron (completing a hand by stealing): Any time you need one more tile
to win, you can claim the current discard if it completes your hand by selecting"Ron."
Tsumo (completing a hand with a self-drawn tile): Any time you need one more tile to win and you draw a tile that completes your hand, you can select"Tsumo."
When you win by ron, the opponent who discarded the winning tile pays you the resulting points. When you win by tsumo, your three opponents pay the resulting points.

pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_mjrule17..en: In order to declare a victory (ron or tsumo), your hand must be worth at least
1 yaku. This means it is possible to meet the 14-tile requirement of 4 groups
of 3-tile sets and a pair, but still be unable to win.
You cannot win by stealing a tile (ron) if you had discarded that tile previously in that round. You can, however, still win through self-draw (tsumo).
Additionally, if you can win by declaring Ron but choose instead not to steal, you will be unable to declare Ron on any discard until the next turn.

Note: The peacock belongs to the bamboo suit.

pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_mjrule4.d.en: Hand: This region contains the tiles you are using to construct your winning hand. Tiles you want to keep will remain here.

pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_mjrule5.d.en: DiscardArea: The region below the player name is the discard area. You can get an idea of the other players' hands by looking atwhat they discard.
MeldArea: The region to the right of your hand is your meld area. Sets made from
cannot take them apart to change up your hand. Remember, your melds canbe seenby everyone!

pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_mjrule6.d.en: A Note on Stealing Tiles: A hand that has no exposed melds is called a "concealed hand." It is generally considered smarter play to keep your hand concealed for as long as you can, so melding (stealing) isn't always therightmove.

pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_mjrule7.d.en: Dealer: The dealer startsoffeach game,and the positionrotateseachround.

When you win a game as the dealer, you earn more points than usual; conversely, if the dealer wins off your discard, you pay more. If you win a hand as the dealer (or if the game ends in a draw), you remain the dealer until anotherplayerwins.
Dora: In the center area, there are tiles that represent the dora. Only one is revealed atthe start,butmorecanbeflipped to createpointbonuses.

pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_mjrule8.d.en: The sets you need to collect are divided into chi, pon, and kan:
Kan: Four-of-a-kind of the same tile.
Pair: Two of the same tile.

pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_mjrule9.d.en: Tips for Beginners Mahjong can be overwhelming for new players. Here are a few suggested hands to aim for when you're getting started:
AllSimples Simply discard any tiles that are not 2-8 of a suit. If Kuitan is in use, you areabletofreelystealdiscards,makingthisoneofthemostaccessible ways to win.
Dragon Triplet or Prevailing Wind/Seat Wind You canwin with any tile combination aslong asyou have at least one triplet of a Dragon, your seat Wind, or the round Wind.

pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_mjyaku00..en: A concealed hand composed entirely of straights and a valueless pair. Also, the hand must be ready on an open-ended wait. (Example: Have 7 and 8 of a given suit and get 6 or 9)
Uses suit tiles 2 through 8 to make four sets and one pair.

pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_mjyaku01..en: A concealed hand with identical straights (same suit and same 3-number sequence).
Ready Hand (Richi): A concealed hand that a player chooses to lock. Upon a win, ura-dora are revealed for each visible dora,increasing potential for points.

pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_mjyaku02..en: One-Shot (lppatsu) A hand completed within one turn of declaring riichi. But ippatsu is canceled ifanyexposedmeld isdeclared.
A triplet (or quad) of white, green, or red dragon tiles.

pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_mjyaku03..en: A triplet (or quad) of the round wind or your seat wind.
Last Tile Draw (Haitei): A hand completed by drawing the last tile from the wall.
Last Tile Discard (Houtei): A hand completed with the last tile discarded by an opponent.

pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_mjyaku04..en: Dead Wall Draw (Rinshan Kaihou): A hand completed using a drawn tile when declaring "Kan."
Robbing a Quad (Chankan): A hand completed using the tile another player used to upgrade a pon to a kan.

pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_mjyaku05..en: A hand with four triplets and one pair.
All sets include a 1, 9, or honor tile. Concealed: 2 han. Exposed: 1 han.

pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_mjyaku06..en: Sequences of 123, 456, and 789 in the same suit. Concealed: 2 han. Exposed: 1 han.
A concealed hand of 7 pairs. All seven pairs must be unique.

pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_mjyaku07..en: Three straights of the same number sequence, one in each suit. Concealed:2han.Exposed:1 han.
A triplet or quad of the Wind tile that is both the round wind and your seat wind.

pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_mjyaku08..en: Three triplets consisting of self-drawn tiles. You cannot call ron to form the third triplet. All three triplets must be concealed.
All triplets or quads of 1s, 9s, and honors.

pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_mjyaku09..en: A hand with any two dragon triplets and using the third dragon as a pair.
A hand with three triplets of the same number, one in each suit.

pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_mjyaku10..en: A hand with three quads that are either concealed or exposed.
DoubleRiichi: When you declare riichi on your first discard.

pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_mjyaku11..en: All sets include a 1 or a 9. Concealed: 3 han. Exposed: 2 han.
A hand consisting of only one suit and any combination of honors. Concealed: 3 han.Exposed:2 han.

pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_mjyaku12..en: A concealed hand with two ldentical Sequences.This scoring element takesprecedence over SevenPairs.

pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_mjyaku13..en: Terminal and Honor Discards (Nagashi Mangan): A hand formed when the round is a draw. In order to qualify, you must have not discarded any number tiles 2 through 8, and you must not have formed any exposed melds. Additionally, no other player must have claimed any of your terminal/honor discards.

pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_mjyaku14..en: A hand consisting ofone suit. Concealed: 6 han. Exposed: 5 han.

pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_mjyaku15..en: Four triplets consisting of self-drawn tiles.You cannot call ron to form the fourthtriplet.All four tripletsmustbeconcealed.

pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_mjyaku16..en: A hand with one triplet each of white, green, and red dragons.
A hand consisting entirely of green tiles (only green dragons and 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8 of Bamboo tiles).

pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_mjyaku17..en: A hand with one of each terminal and honor tile, plus a duplicate of any
A hand with any three wind triplets and a pair of winds.

pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_mjyaku18..en: A hand consisting of only 1 and 9 tiles to form 4 sets and 1 pair.
A concealed hand consisting of seven pairs of dots 2 through 8.

pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_mjyaku19..en: A hand consisting of four quads that are either concealed or exposed.
A concealed Full Flush with three 1s, three 9s, one each of 2 through 8,

pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_mjyaku20..en: Heavenly Hand (Tenhou): The dealer has a completed hand with his initial 14 tiles.
Earthly Hand (Chiihou): A non-dealer completes a hand on his first draw, but only if another player has not claimed a discard.

pausepar_pause_en/picture/rule_mjyaku21..en: Four Concealed Triplets with Single Wait (Suu Ankou Tanki):
Same as Four Concealed Triplets, except that you finish the hand by making a pair.
